source.title: When Language Representations Interact: Separability and Cross-Lingual Effects in LLMs
source.authors: Boris Marinov; Angira Sharma; C. D. de Witt; P. Torr; A. Calinescu; Jia-Lin Yu

record.tranche_reason: The study examines language-concept geometry and interventions, but does not test superposition, capacity pressure, SAE features, or whether superposed features are one-dimensional.
record.gate_note: The paper reports measurements of bilingual concept directions and their geometry. These results do not establish that sparse, overcomplete features are stored by superposition, or test any of the listed versions. Related findings are recorded under fits_no_version. The paper's discussion of intervention effects is about language-concept directions, not an evaluation of superposition.
record.test_reason: The study applies the linear-representation/causal-inner-product framework to bilingual language concepts in three LLMs. It measures direction association, near-orthogonality under a whitened inner product, family simplex geometry, and logit shifts from additive interventions. It does not study sparse overcomplete features, superposition in toy models, capacity-driven polysemanticity, neuron-level polysemanticity, SAEs, or whether superposed units are 1-D. Its near-orthogonality is between a small set (31) of concept directions in a high-dimensional space, not features outnumbering dimensions, and the authors note near-orthogonality is expected after whitening. Superposition is not mentioned. Engels et al. (multi-dimensional features) is only cited.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that language identity behaves approximately as a separable factor under causal-geometric diagnostics, with structured overlap reflecting linguistic similarity and family hierarchy. They also report logit-level intervention signal but limited generation-level control.
record.recipe_differences: The study applies covariance-adjusted causal-geometric measurements to bilingual language concepts and additive interventions; it does not use the toy-network superposition method.
record.method_sensitivity: The authors report that intervention effects are heterogeneous across language pairs and that generation-level control is sensitive to tokenization and context.

fits_no_version.finding: Bilingual contrasts show right-skewed projections onto leave-one-out concept directions versus near-zero random baselines (Qwen3-4B; plots for other models).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Language contrasts in LLMs admit stable approximately linear directions.

fits_no_version.finding: Under the causal inner product, most bilingual directions not sharing a language are near-orthogonal. Deviations track linguistic similarity and German–capitalization association.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Language-concept directions are largely separable with structured, linguistically aligned overlap.

fits_no_version.finding: Same-family languages form simplex-like structures approximately orthogonal to the family direction across three models.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Language identity is encoded hierarchically, in line with categorical-hierarchy geometry.

fits_no_version.finding: Additive interventions give approximately monotonic log-odds shifts, but generation-level control is limited.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Linear language directions carry logit-level causal signal without reliable steering.

record.peer_reviewed: ICML 2026 Workshop on Trustworthy AI for Good (AI4GOOD)
record.problems: The study uses bilingual translations as approximate counterfactual pairs rather than ground-truth interventions, and notes that tokenization artifacts cannot be fully mitigated. It covers only two Indo-European language families and Latin-alphabet languages, with limited layers, prompts, and intervention strengths. It reports no uncertainty estimates in the text.
record.rows_left_out: No separately quantified figure values were extracted where the text provides only plots or qualitative descriptions; the reported aggregate findings are represented in the rows above.

untested.parts: Toy networks, sparse features exceeding dimensions, sparsity-dependent phase transition, superposition geometry.
Capacity competition as the cause of polysemanticity; dedicated vs shared dimensions.
Features distributed across neurons in LLMs; SAE recovery of sparse features.
Completeness, stability or canonicity of SAE features.
Whether superposed features are 1-D or multi-dimensional.

record.verdict_notes: Relation could arguably be cites_only rather than discusses. Superposition is never discussed; the paper only cites Engels et al. on non-1-D features as a limit of linear control. Rows contain no numeric values, only plot descriptions. No uncertainty is reported.

versions.untested_parts: Toy networks, sparse overcomplete features, and a sparsity-dependent superposition transition or geometry.
Whether polysemanticity results from capacity competition or whether features receive dedicated versus shared dimensions.
Whether polysemanticity arises without capacity pressure or is evidence for superposition.
Whether LLM features are distributed across neurons or recovered by sparse autoencoders.
Whether dictionary features are complete, stable, or canonical units of model representation.
Whether the units superposed are one-dimensional rather than multidimensional features.

rows.subject: Qwen3-4B
rows.operation_detail: Projected counterfactual and random word-pair differences onto estimated concept directions.

conditions.value: 31 sets: 28 bilingual contrasts plus 3 non-linguistic concepts

rows.baseline: Random word differences have mean projection near zero.
rows.value: Counterfactual pairs exhibit a pronounced right-skewed distribution; the paper describes stable linear signal across a range of language contrasts.
rows.note: This measures language-concept direction association, not feature superposition.
rows.check: Linked correctly to none. It measures linear concept-direction association, not superposition.

rows.subject: Qwen3-4B
rows.operation_detail: Computed causal inner products between estimated concept directions.

conditions.value: 31 concepts: 28 bilingual contrasts plus 3 non-linguistic concepts

rows.value: Most bilingual concept pairs that do not share a language are described as near-orthogonal; the directions are not exactly orthogonal, and deviations are said to align with linguistic relationships.
rows.note: The paper cautions that near-orthogonality can arise in high-dimensional spaces after whitening.
rows.check: Near-orthogonality of 31 directions under a causal inner product is not overlapping storage of more features than dimensions. Not V1 or V4 evidence.

rows.subject: Llama-3-8B, Mistral-7B-v0.3, Qwen3-4B
rows.operation_detail: Analyzed family-level and language-specific directions in the causally whitened representation space.
rows.value: Across all models, languages in the same family are reported to form simplex-like structures; for Germanic languages, the simplex is described as approximately orthogonal to the family direction.
rows.note: The paper reports this as hierarchical language geometry, not as a result about overcomplete feature storage.
rows.check: Hierarchical simplex geometry of language directions. Not the toy-model superposition geometry of V1. Evidence is plots only.

rows.subject: Qwen3-4B
rows.operation_detail: Compared projections of French and Spanish Wikipedia contexts onto bilingual concept directions.
rows.baseline: Off-target concepts, including male⇒female and German⇒English, show substantial overlap.
rows.value: Directions involving French or Spanish produce strong distributional separation; Italian⇒Portuguese also produces non-trivial separation.
rows.note: This is a context-projection result, not a measurement of feature superposition.
rows.check: Context-projection separation. Unrelated to any version.

rows.subject: Qwen3-4B
rows.operation_detail: Added estimated concept directions to context representations and measured next-token log-odds shifts.

conditions.value: Simple categorical concepts and bilingual contrasts

rows.measure: Log-odds shifts for target counterfactual tokens
rows.value: The paper reports systematic, approximately monotonic shifts in the expected direction as intervention strength increases.
rows.note: The authors describe these as diagnostic logit-level effects, not reliable generation control.
rows.check: Steering logit shifts with no measure of the claim's behaviour.
